record.original_question: We will say that g(x) is a rearrangement of f (x) if m{x : g(x) < y} = m{x : f (x) < y} for all y ∈ R, where m is Lebesgue measure and f and g are defined on some finite interval I. What are those functions f (x) for which f ′ (x) is a rearrangement f (x)? Obvious examples of such functions are f (x) = kex on any interval and f (x) = k sin x on [0, 12 π]. What others are there? How about other ‘differential rearrangements’ than f ′ (z) ∼ f (x)? (L. A. Rubel)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $I \subset \mathbb{R}$ be a finite interval and let $m$ denote Lebesgue measure. Two measurable functions $f, g : I \to \mathbb{R}$ are called rearrangements of one another if
$$m\{x \in I : g(x) < y\} = m\{x \in I : f(x) < y\} \quad \text{for every } y \in \mathbb{R}.$$

(a) Characterize all (sufficiently smooth) functions $f : I \to \mathbb{R}$ with the property that $f'$ is a rearrangement of $f$ on $I$. Examples include $f(x) = k e^{x}$ on any finite interval and $f(x) = k \sin x$ on $[0, \tfrac{1}{2}\pi]$; determine whether there are essentially different examples and give a complete description.

(b) More generally, study "differential rearrangement" relations: for which functions $f$ and which differential operators $D$ (other than $D = d/dx$) is $Df$ a rearrangement of $f$?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search for Rubel's problem on functions whose derivative is an equimeasurable rearrangement of themselves returned only general results on rearrangement inequalities and no specific resolution or partial progress on this characterization problem. No published source could be located confirming the problem has been solved or systematically addressed, so its current status is unclear.

status_evidence.title: A General Integral Inequality for the Derivative of an Equimeasurable Rearrangement
status_evidence.snippet: Paper on derivatives of equimeasurable rearrangements (1976), but does not address Rubel's specific characterization question.
status_evidence.claim: General literature on rearrangement derivatives exists but does not solve the posed characterization.

status_evidence.title: A Short Course on Rearrangement Inequalities (Burchard)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of rearrangement inequalities; no mention of the specific 'f' is a rearrangement of f' problem.
status_evidence.claim: Standard surveys on rearrangements do not record a solution to this problem.
